sections.h2: Who sends the bill for a Greensboro home
sections.html:
Guilford County, not the City of Greensboro, mails the bill, and the city levy rides on the same statement. The Guilford County Tax Department keeps counters at 400 W. Market St. in Greensboro and 325 E. Russell Ave. in High Point, both open 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. Monday through Friday.

Dial 336-641-4814 about values and appeals. To arrange paying a balance in full before the delinquent date, use 336-641-3363. Greensboro sets its own levy, and the county's table shows it on a separate line.

Lenders that escrow request your bill each summer and send you a notice. Under North Carolina law, getting the tax paid is still the owner's job, so if the lender named on that notice is not yours, forward it to the right servicer.

For 2026-2027 the countywide rate is 0.78950 and the City of Greensboro rate is 0.79850, for a total of 1.58800 under rate code 01. Rates are fractions of $1 for each $100 of value.

Code 01 covers most city parcels. Parcels in the Dunleath and College Hill historic districts and the downtown improvement district carry an extra district charge, so read the code on your bill. A $30 vehicle fee also applies in Greensboro and is neither discounted nor penalized.

The law froze use of the 2026 reappraisal values for one year, so bills for the fiscal year that began July 1, 2026 rest on the older values. The moratorium covers the county's revaluation process. It does not stop local governments from changing their rates.

  • Greensboro adopted its fiscal year 2026-27 budget in June, with a total city rate of 79.85 cents.
  • The city describes that as a 12.6-cent adjustment on current property values, not on the new reappraisal values.
  • The updated values are paused until January 1, 2027, and are expected to feed the budget year that begins July 1, 2027.

Your new notice of value does not set this year's bill. It still matters, because if the value is wrong the appeal clock runs on it, and an appeal that stays open now is considered for the 2027 tax year.

sections.h2: Due dates and how to pay
sections.html:
The bill is due September 1 and stays free of interest through January 5 (G.S. 105-360). After that, interest is 2% for the first month and 0.75% on the first of every month that follows.

  • Discount: Guilford County and Greensboro each give 1.0% off for payment before September 1.
  • Online, or by phone at (336) 203-7795: 1.85% processing charge and a $2 transaction fee.
  • At a tax office counter: cash and checks are free, while a card carries 2.35% and $2.
  • Mail: Guilford County Tax Department, P.O. Box 70939, Charlotte, NC 28272-0939.

The USPS postmark fixes the date of a mailed payment, and proving it was on time falls to you. The county phones about payment only when a bill is delinquent, and gift cards are never accepted.

Send the appeal to the Guilford County Tax Department. Filings for 2026 are accepted through December 31, 2026, and filings for 2027 through May 17, 2027. The online portal opens January 1, 2027.

If you already appealed the reappraisal value, you do not need to refile, because that appeal carries into tax year 2027.

For a paper form, hand it to a postal clerk for a hand-cancelled postmark. A mailbox drop can be stamped the next day with no proof, and anything postmarked after May 17 is rejected. Before the portal opens, request a form at taxreval@guilfordcountync.gov.

The board hears whatever staff cannot settle. The next stop is the state Property Tax Commission, with notice due 30 days after the board mails its decision (G.S. 105-290). Personal property is a separate track with its own 30-day window from the notice date.

Greensboro homeowners may use any of three state programs, with a June 1 filing deadline each year. Mail applications to Guilford County Tax Department, PO Box 3138, Greensboro, NC 27402, or carry them to either tax office.

  • Elderly or disabled exclusion: $25,000 or half the value, whichever is more, off the home of a qualifying 65-plus or disabled owner whose gross income stays under $38,800. One application is enough.
  • Circuit breaker: the tax is held to 4% or 5% of income, using caps of $38,800 and $58,200, after five years of owning and living in the home. It is renewed annually.
  • Disabled veteran exclusion: the first $45,000 of value, with no age or income test, applied for once.

Only one program per owner is allowed. A late application is still reviewed if it arrives at least one week before the last equalization board meeting in December. Questions go to 336-641-3320 or 336-641-7911. A circuit breaker owner who sells owes the last three years of deferred tax, with interest, on the sale date.

Interest starts, collection begins at once, and the tax stays a lien on the parcel. Tools include wage and bank garnishment, levies on personal property, attachment of state refunds and lottery winnings, and foreclosure on real estate.

Under G.S. 105-355 the lien dates from the listing date and includes penalties and costs. A foreclosure action under G.S. 105-374 ends at a courthouse-door auction, and redemption before confirmation requires paying taxes, interest, penalties and costs. Guilford holds no tax lien sales.

Before listing, ask the tax department for the figures on the current bill. A deferred balance under a relief program is a separate item, so ask for it by name. A cash buyer will still expect the title to be clear, so the tax has to be settled at or before closing.

Greensboro has 308,667 residents and 123,984 households, averaging 2.29 people. About 50.5% of homes are owner-occupied, so owners and renters are nearly even and a sale often has a landlord on one side. The middle value of an owner's home is $244,800, middle gross rent is $1,172, and middle owner costs with a mortgage are $1,447 a month, a baseline to hold against your own tax line. When you list, have the current bill, your rate code and any relief approval letter ready for the buyer's agent.

faqs.q: Which government mails the Greensboro tax statement?
faqs.a: Guilford County. Its tax department bills the county and city levies together from counters at 400 W. Market St., Greensboro, and 325 E. Russell Ave., High Point.

faqs.q: What total rate does a city parcel carry?
faqs.a: Rate code 01 totals 1.58800 for 2026-2027, made of 0.78950 countywide plus 0.79850 for Greensboro. Historic and downtown districts add more.
Yes. Guilford County and Greensboro each allow a 1.0% discount for paying before September 1.

faqs.q: Is an appeal still possible after the moratorium?
faqs.a: Yes. Guilford accepts 2026 appeals through December 31, 2026, and 2027 appeals through May 17, 2027, with its online portal starting January 1, 2027. Earlier appeals stay active.

faqs.q: Does Guilford County auction tax liens to investors?
faqs.a: No. The tax department conducts no tax lien sales, though it enforces collection with garnishment and real estate foreclosure.
